statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail holds at 7 because the cash-open decline stayed retraced: NQ trades mid-upper in its day range above the prior close while VIX decays toward its session low, even as stress stays high across the energy, inflation and trade channels.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON, with a narrow flagged window from 17:00 to 18:00 UTC around the US 3-year note auction, the one scheduled checkpoint able to reactivate the rates channel that accompanied the morning decline. Tail remains well below the block threshold because mean reversion has demonstrably worked in both directions this session.
headline: NQ holds its retracement above the prior close as semiconductors gain over 2% against a 1.1% Dow decline
body: NQ futures trade near 29,578.75, up 0.05% on the session, inside a 29,425.00 to 29,764.75 day range. The downside leg that lifted tail to 15 two hours ago has stayed retraced rather than resumed: price sits above the 29,544.15 prior close and in the upper half of the range, roughly 150 points off the session low. That is the reason tail holds at 7. The structure that matters for this strategy is repeated extension after failed retracements, and the observed path is the opposite of it. The cash index confirms the read, with the Nasdaq-100 at 29,573.36, up 0.10%, inside a 29,400.70 to 29,655.73 range. Volatility continues to decay alongside the recovery. VIX at 15.34 is up just 0.26% and sits near the bottom of its 15.28 to 15.94 day range, having given back the morning spike entirely. Index internals remain sharply split, which is what keeps the dominant mode at mixed rather than trend-up or trend-down. SOXX is up 2.27% at 531.64 after Qualcomm's multi-generation custom-silicon agreement with Amazon Web Services lifted the stock as much as 9.5%, while the Dow is down 1.07% at 52,844.49 and the S&P 500 is down 0.38%. Energy leads sectors, up more than 1%. That combination is rotation into semiconductors against broad cyclical weakness, not one-way index pressure, and the Nasdaq's outperformance is being driven by a single-name catalyst rather than by index-level trend. The rates channel is stable: the 10-year yield near 4.786% is roughly unchanged on the day, and the H.15 release for 3 September had the 2-year at 4.34% against the 10-year at 4.77%. Stress stays in the high band at 70. WTI near $92.19 is up 0.77% and Brent near $97.54 rose as high as $99.46, at roughly three-month highs after further Houthi strikes halted operations at several Saudi energy facilities, with the outage duration unresolved. Crude has added roughly $25 since early July. Canada's retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% on about $20 billion of U.S. goods took effect today, keeping the North American trade channel live, and reporting places CME FedWatch odds of a rate increase at the coming Federal Reserve meeting near 58 to 60 percent, which is an unusual configuration for a market this close to a CPI print. The one release already inside this session was the New York Fed's August Survey of Consumer Expectations, published at 15:00 UTC, which showed one-year inflation expectations unchanged at 3.6%, the three-year measure down to 3.2%, the five-year measure at 3.0%, and mean unemployment expectations at 44.4%, the highest since April 2020. Steady inflation expectations alongside a softer labour-market read is a benign combination for the rates channel and is consistent with the observed recovery. The next scheduled checkpoint is the US 3-year note auction at 17:00 UTC, which is the flagged window. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was collected at 12:18 UTC and is outside the 90-minute freshness limit, so this assessment rests on the independently fetched live sources listed below rather than on that delayed snapshot.

lookbackSummary: Across the last 24 hours the assessment stayed in the EA_ON band with tail between 5 and 10 until the 14:00 UTC slot, where it stepped up to 15 on an observed cash-open downside leg that left NQ near the session low, then fell back to 8 once that leg was fully retraced. Stress climbed steadily from the low 60s during Monday's Labor Day holiday session to a peak of 72 by early Tuesday afternoon as crude extended on the Saudi facility strikes and the North American trade channel reopened. The dominant mode sat at mixed for most of the window because cross-asset signals kept diverging from Nasdaq price action, turning to trend-down only for the single hour that carried the decline. The 09:00 UTC slot has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The horizon starts with the cash-open decline still retraced and conditional tail at 7, then steps up around the 17:00 UTC 3-year auction and again into the 20:00 UTC closing auction, where rebalancing flow meets unusually wide sector dispersion. Conditional tail falls to the floor of the horizon overnight through the Asian session, with the 07:00 UTC European open on 9 September and the 13:30 UTC US cash open as the next flow checkpoints; the hour after that open carries the horizon peak at 13, because opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks is the specific structure that overwhelms mean reversion. Every slot stays inside the EA_ON band. Three channels could force a step change in either direction: Middle East energy headlines, where the duration of the halted Saudi facility operations is unresolved; the North American trade dispute after Canada's tariffs took effect today; and rate expectations, with reporting placing hike odds for the coming Federal Reserve meeting near 58 to 60 percent into Thursday's PPI and Friday's CPI. Stress stays in the high band throughout because none of those channels is resolved, while confidence decays overnight as the live evidence base ages and recovers once the 9 September cash session provides fresh structure.
